questions.q: Which is the main UK body that enforces competition law?
questions.why: It looks at mergers, cartels and dominant firms.

questions.q: Which is most likely to breach competition law?
options: A dominant firm unfairly driving out a small rival
A firm growing by selling better products
questions.why: Being large is not the problem. Abusing that position is.

questions.q: Being given strategic market status is a finding of wrongdoing.
questions.why: It gives the CMA power to set rules for that firm.

questions.q: Which is a likely benefit of competition policy?
questions.why: Rivalry puts pressure on prices, costs and quality.

questions.q: Which is a cost of competition policy?
questions.why: There are also risks of blocking useful mergers.

questions.q: Explain why blocking a merger may not always benefit consumers.

ideas.label: The merger could have brought economies of scale
So prices could have been lower, or more could have been spent on innovation

questions.model: The merged firm might have gained economies of scale. These lower costs could have been passed on in lower prices or funded more research.
questions.why: Bigger can mean cheaper, if savings are passed on.

tests.answer: The merger could bring economies of scale, which might be passed on in lower prices.
It could bring economies of scale.
